newsitem.title: USA: P.S. New Mexico choice plan for natgas approved.
newsitem.headline: P.S. New Mexico choice plan for natgas approved.

text.p: Public Service Co of New Mexico (PNM) said Tuesday New Mexico's regulatory commission approved a plan to allow consumers to choose their natural gas supplier.
The plan will allow all PNM's residential gas customers and small businesses using less than 10,000 therms annually to select a supplier other than PNM beginning in December 1997.
Billing, metering, and other customer service functions will still be administered by PNM.
Because PNM's gas services unit does not make a profit on the gas it buys for its sales customers, the plan is not expected to have any effect on earnings, the company said in a statement.
The commission order allows PNM to recover costs prudently incurred in launching and supporting the choice program.
PNM now serves about 368,000 residential and 30,000 commercial gas customers.
The company has also offered a plan for commission approval that would allow gas sales customers to either choose a fixed annual gas cost or level gas costs over a period of several months.
A separate gas rate case, also ordered in February, is scheduled to be filed by PNM on Sept 2.
PNM is a combined gas and electric utility serving about 1.2 million people in New Mexico.
